title: Module Summary: Foundations of Web Development

concepts.name: Browser
concepts.description: Software that requests web resources, interprets HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and renders interactive pages for users.

concepts.name: Server
concepts.description: A computer or program that responds to network requests by returning data, files, or application responses.

concepts.name: Client-server model
concepts.description: A network pattern where a client sends requests and a server returns responses.

concepts.name: HTTP request
concepts.description: A message from a client asking a server for a resource or action.

concepts.name: HTTP response
concepts.description: A server message that returns status information and requested content or data.

concepts.name: HTML document
concepts.description: A structured document that defines the content and semantic structure of a web page.

concepts.name: CSS stylesheet
concepts.description: A file or block of CSS rules that controls presentation, layout, and visual styling.

concepts.name: JavaScript file
concepts.description: A script file that adds behavior, state changes, and interactivity to a web page.

concepts.name: URL
concepts.description: A web address that identifies the location and access method for a resource.

concepts.name: Domain name
concepts.description: A human-readable name that maps to an internet address through DNS.

concepts.name: DNS lookup
concepts.description: The process of resolving a domain name to the IP address of a server.

concepts.name: IP address
concepts.description: A numeric network address used to locate a device or server on the internet.

concepts.name: Hosting
concepts.description: Providing server infrastructure where a website or application can be accessed by users.

concepts.name: Deployment
concepts.description: Publishing code or files to an environment where users can access the application.

concepts.name: Static site
concepts.description: A website served as prebuilt files without server-side rendering for each request.

concepts.name: Production environment
concepts.description: The live environment where real users access a website or application.

concepts.name: Code editor
concepts.description: A tool for writing, navigating, and editing source code.

concepts.name: Terminal
concepts.description: A command-line interface for running programs and development commands.

concepts.name: Browser developer tools
concepts.description: Built-in browser tools for inspecting HTML, CSS, JavaScript, network requests, storage, and performance.

concepts.name: Version control
concepts.description: A system for tracking changes to files over time and coordinating work across versions or contributors.

concepts.name: Local development server
concepts.description: A server run on a developer’s machine to preview and test a web project locally.

concepts.name: Debugging workflow
concepts.description: A systematic process for observing, isolating, and fixing errors in code or behavior.

concepts.name: Module
concepts.description: A self-contained unit of code or content with a clear responsibility.

concepts.name: Separation of concerns
concepts.description: The practice of keeping different responsibilities in separate files, components, functions, or layers.

concepts.name: File organization
concepts.description: The structure used to group project files so their roles and relationships are understandable.

concepts.name: Component boundary
concepts.description: The line defining what a component owns, exposes, and depends on.

concepts.name: Reusable code
concepts.description: Code written so it can be used in more than one place without duplication.

concepts.name: Project structure
concepts.description: The overall organization of folders, files, modules, assets, and configuration in a project.
